title: French and Creole songs, including a Haitian revolution song
summary: Alice tries to recall old songs and recites a Creole song about the Haitian revolution and hunger.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did you know any little songs, French songs or folk songs when you were young? Do you remember any of those songs you heard?
Well, I was just telling George, I said, George, as many as I knew. I just can't remember nothing. Now, I can remember, but that's not French. It's, uh, how is Jamaican? Jamaica. Jamaica?
That's, uh, Jamaica. You told me.
In Haiti, from Haiti. From Haiti? Haiti. Well, that's a Creole. That's a Creole.
They have a Creole down there. Haiti?

Uh-huh. Yes, I believe it is, because I'll tell you, the French song that I know is mostly mixed up. Uh-huh. Toe tae is siens, dee puis plus dee en zan, tapez, we'll tapez, we'll that's Creole. Uh-huh. Tapez soufer de la plus grande misère, mangez tes chers, pas tes gagnants l'argent, that's Creole. Uh-huh. La peinte est tuée, déjà beaucoup de merde, that's Creole. Uh-huh. Uh-huh.
And what is that song about?

Well, it was when they had the revolution in Haiti, Haiti as they call it. Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And they had Prince Geoffrey, and he had to come to do for them, you know, to help them out, because they were starving. Starving. The mothers were starving. You notice, they say, la feinte, la feinte est tuée, la feinte est tuée, that means hunger kills the many mothers. Uh-huh.
And do you know any other songs that you remember from way back? Uh-huh. It's hard for me to bring them.
